topics.label: Introduction to the initiation and resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing the overarching theme of how established immune cells and molecules coordinate to initiate and resolve inflammatory reactions.

topics.label: Innate recognition of pathogens and damage by pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms by which the innate immune system senses microbial products and tissue damage using various pattern recognition receptors and downstream signaling pathways.

topics.label: Cellular recruitment, trafficking, and systemic inflammatory responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how sentinel cell activation directs the migration and trafficking of leukocytes through blood and lymphatic vessels, as well as the systemic hazards of hyperactivated inflammation.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammatory states
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the mechanisms used to shut down acute inflammation and repair injured tissue, alongside the persistent conditions that lead to chronic inflammation and granulomas.

topics.label: Closing and next lecture preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with closing remarks and a preview of the next topic.
